_about: Held-out benchmark for the 2026-11-11 plan. scenarios.json is the dev set that SKILL.md wording is iterated against; nobody tunes against this file.
Frozen by commit before any run. A later change to a key needs a CHANGELOG entry and a baseline re-run.
Keys: {"band": "Undetermined"} means the last rubric run must be Undetermined. {"accepted": [...]} means the last run's top (or co-top on a tied conservative bound) must be in the set.
"failure" lists shared remote stores for the two single-instance, restart-tolerant cases; a top pick from that list is the demo's error in another domain.

cases.user_message: Which message broker should the new service use?
cases.why: No stated requirement (volume, ordering, retention, existing infra) separates these; any ranking comes from priors alone.

cases.user_message: Pick a bundler for the web app.
cases.why: Nothing stated about the app, its framework, legacy plugins or build targets. All three ship working web builds (each tool's own getting-started docs).

cases.user_message: What retry policy should the outbound HTTP client use?
cases.why: Whether the calls are idempotent is unstated, and that decides whether retrying is safe at all (RFC 9110 section 9.2.2).

cases.user_message: Which primary key format for the new table?
cases.why: Single-writer vs multi-region generation, sortability and exposure of the key are all unstated; each candidate wins under some of them.

cases.user_message: Pick a queue for the background job runner. Hard requirement: no new infrastructure, Postgres is the only service we run. Preference: jobs retry with backoff.
cases.why: NATS and Pulsar are new services and fail the hard requirement. SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED is documented for exactly this queue pattern (PostgreSQL docs, SELECT, 'The Locking Clause').

cases.user_message: Where should feature flags live? Hard requirement: a flag must flip without a deploy. Preference: no new vendor.
candidates: Database table with an admin page

accepted: Database table with an admin page

cases.why: Environment variables need a restart or redeploy to change, failing the hard requirement. LaunchDarkly passes it but is a new vendor (soft). The table passes both.

cases.user_message: Session store for the internal admin tool. It runs as one instance, we have no database yet, and users logging in again after a deploy is explicitly fine. Hard requirement: no new service to operate.
cases.why: One instance and restart tolerance are stated, so a shared store solves a problem the user said they do not have, and both shared stores are new services (hard fail). Flask/Django/Express session docs all offer in-process memory for this shape.

cases.user_message: Rate limiting for the webhook receiver. One process, no replicas planned, and counters may reset on restart. Hard requirement: no network hop on the hot path.
cases.why: Both shared options add a network hop per request, failing the hard requirement. Token bucket is the standard algorithm (RFC 2697/2698 describe it for traffic policing).

cases.user_message: Bundler for a TypeScript library we publish to npm. Hard requirement: emit both ESM and CJS with type declarations from one config. Preference: as little config as possible.
cases.why: tsup emits esm+cjs and .d.ts from one command (`--format esm,cjs --dts`, tsup docs). Vite library mode needs a dts plugin; webpack needs a declaration setup and a config file. Only tsup satisfies hard and soft at once.

cases.user_message: Retry policy for calls to the payment provider. Hard requirement: the charge call is not idempotent and the provider has no idempotency keys, so a duplicate retry double-charges. Preference: keep it simple.
cases.why: Retrying a non-idempotent request without an idempotency key can duplicate the side effect (RFC 9110 section 9.2.2; Stripe's idempotent-requests docs exist precisely to make retries safe).

cases.user_message: Where should application logs go? Hard requirement: we run on Kubernetes with an existing Loki stack and no new log vendor. Preference: structured JSON lines.
cases.why: Datadog is a new vendor (hard fail). Pod-local files are lost on reschedule and bypass the collector. Kubernetes logging architecture docs describe stdout/stderr as the path the node agent (here Promtail/Alloy) collects.

cases.user_message: Primary key format for events written in several regions and merged later. Hard requirement: keys are generated without coordination between regions. Preference: roughly time-sortable.
cases.why: Auto-increment needs a coordinating sequence (hard fail). UUIDv4 is coordination-free but random, so unsorted (soft miss). ULID is coordination-free and lexicographically time-sortable (ULID spec).
